answer.rationale: The release went out 2 hours ago and p99 write latency started climbing 90 minutes ago, consistent with memory_b1 where a rollback cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact. Settlement is at daily peak so writes are heavy; a regional failover or capacity add would take longer and risks more disruption. A rollback restores the prior stable build immediately, preserving customer writes and sustained availability. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing are for dependency or read-path issues, neither of which applies here. Memory_b6 would confirm that if the release had already passed canary gates it should be stable, so the regression is in the general rollout — another reason to roll back.
